messages.subject: Priors on growth curve intercept and slope
parts:
Greetings,

I am running a growth curve model in "blavaan", estimating an intercept and slope.  I would like to override the default priors for the means of these two growth factors.   I have added the line iprior <- dpriors(alpha="dnorm(500,.01)"), but when I run this using the 'bgrowth' command in "blavaan", it doesn't seem to change the priors, and when I run it in 'bcfa', I don't get any estimates for the means of the growth factors.  Any help would be appreciated.  Here is the code and output using 'bcfa'

BayesLinGCM <- '
# intercept and slope with fixed coefficients
i =~ 1*Girls_MathPV1_99m + 1*Girls_MathPV1_03m + 1*Girls_MathPV1_07m + 1*Girls_MathPV1_11m + 1*Girls_MathPV1_15m
s1 =~ 0*Girls_MathPV1_99m + 4*Girls_MathPV1_03m + 8*Girls_MathPV1_07m + 12*Girls_MathPV1_11m + 16*Girls_MathPV1_15m


'

#  Fit quadratic growth curve model and obtain predicted values
fitGirlsAchLinBayes <- bcfa(BayesLinGCM, data=newdataGirsAch1,
              target="jags",adapt=5000,save.lvs=TRUE,burnin=1000, sample=25000)
iprior <- dpriors(alpha="dnorm(500,.01)")
summary(fitGirlsAchLinBayes)

David

I think the issue is that you are setting the dprior as an object, but is not assign to the bcfa or bgroiwth functions. And of the bcfa, it will fix the latent means to 0 by default, I think this should work

fitGirlsAchLinBayes <- bgrowth(BayesLinGCM, data=newdataGirsAch1,dp=dpriors(alpha="dnorm(500,.01)"),
              target="jags",adapt=5000,burnin=1000, sample=25000)

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Priors on growth curve intercept and slope
parts:
Hi David,

I think that bgrowth() is the way to go here, or potentially blavaan()
if you need even more flexibility.

If Mauricio's suggestion didn't work, there is also a known bug where
the priors for some "alpha" parameters are pulled from the "nu" slot.
So you might try setting the "nu" prior in dpriors() as well as
"alpha".

If you want to set a prior for an individual parameter (i.e., on one
alpha instead of all the alphas), you can also use the prior()
modifier in your model specification. For an example, see the
"individual parameters" section here:

http://faculty.missouri.edu/~merklee/blavaan/prior.html

Ed
